tools.name: search
tools.description: Search published StatOrigin statistics by indicator, place, industry, or words from the source sentence. Takes one query string (2–120 characters) and returns at most 20 results, each with id, title, and url. The url is the canonical record at https://statorigin.org/stat/{id}. Call fetch with id to

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Read one published statistic by the stat_ id returned from search. Does not retrieve arbitrary URLs. Returns id, title, text, and the canonical StatOrigin url, plus metadata: value, unit, scale, period, region, publisher, the verbatim source quote, the source document URL, and the canonical URL agai

tools.name: get_ranking
tools.description: Read one published country ranking by the slug of its https://statorigin.org/rankings/{slug} page. Example: crude-steel-production-by-country. Returns the comparable period and at most 20 rows. Each row has rank, value, unit, region, publisher, statistic id, and canonical url. If scan_capped is true

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, fetch, get_ranking · Private data: search, fetch · Public sink: get_ranking.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, fetch, get_ranking · Private data: search, fetch · Public sink: get_ranking

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
